source_text: Vetus es, uera si uelimus dicere, tu qui tantum gulae indulges, et merito te priorem iactitas; semper agnosco sapere Esau uenatorem ferarum; ita passim indagandis turdis studes, ita de campo laxissimae disciplinae tuae uenis, ita spiritu deficis. si tibi lenticulam defruto inrufatam obtulero, statim totos primatus tuos uendes; apud te agape in caccabis feruet, fides in culmis calet, spes in ferculis iacet. sed maioris est agape, quia per hanc adulescentes tui cum sororibus dormiunt. appendices scilicet gulae lasciuia atque luxuriae. quam societatem et apostolus sciens cum praemisisset non in ebrietatibus nec in comessationibus, adiunxit nec in cubilibus et libidinibus. ad elogium gulae tuae pertinet, quod duplex apud te praesidentibus honor binis partibus deputatur, cum apostolus duplicem honorem dederit ut et fratribus et praepositis. quis sanctior inter uos, nisi conuiuandi frequentior, nisi obsonandi pollucibilior, nisi calicibus instructior?v merito homines solius animae et carnis spiritalia recusatis. talibus si placerent prophetae, mei non erant. cur ergo non constanter praedicatis: manducemus et bibamus, cras enim moriemur? sicuti nos non dubitamus exerte mandare: ieiunemus fratres et sorores, ne forte cras moriamur. palam disciplinas nostras uindicemus. nos certi sumus eos qui in carne sunt deo placere non posse, non utique in substantia carnis, sed in cura, sed in affectione, sed in operatione, sed in uoluntate. macies non displicet nobis; neque enim ad pondus deus carnem tribuit, sicut nec spiritum ad mensuram. facilius, si forte, per angustam salutis ianuam introibit caro exilior; citius resuscitabitur caro leuior, diutius in sepultura durabit caro aridior. saginentur pugiles et pyctae Olympici. illis ambitio corporis competit, quibus et uires necessariae, et tamen illi quoque xerophagiis inualescunt. sed nostra alia robora aliaeque uires, sicut et alia certamina, quibus non est luctatio aduersus carnem et sanguinem, sed aduersus mundi potestates, aduersus spiritalia malitiae. aduersus haec non carne et sanguine, sed fide et spiritu robusto oportet adsistere. ceterum saginatior Christianus ursis et leoni- - bus forte quam deo erit necessarius, nisi quod et aduersus bestias maciem exercere debebit.
thought_title: Gluttony versus the lean body of faith
orientation: Tertullian is addressing an unspiritual Christian opponent directly, contrasting his gluttonous lifestyle with the fasting discipline he defends.
pass_a_gloss: You are old, if we wish to speak the truth, you who indulge so much in gluttony, and deservedly you boast that you are earlier; I always recognize that you have the taste of Esau the hunter of wild beasts; so you are eager everywhere for tracking thrushes, so you come from the field of your very loose discipline, so you fail in spirit. If I offer you lentil stew reddened with reduced wine, immediately you will sell all your birthrights; among you love-feast boils in pots, faith grows warm in stalks of grain, hope lies in dishes. But love-feast is of greater importance, because through this your young men sleep with sisters. Appendages, of course, of gluttony are wantonness and luxuries. The apostle also knowing this association, when he had first said not in drunkenness nor in revelings, added nor in beds and lusts. To the charge against your gluttony it belongs, that among you double honor is assigned to the presiding elders in two portions, when the apostle gave double honor so that both to brothers and to leaders. Who is holier among you, unless more frequent in banqueting, unless more lavish in providing food, unless better equipped with cups? Deservedly you men of soul alone and flesh refuse spiritual things. If prophets pleased such men, they were not mine. Why therefore do you not consistently proclaim: let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die? Just as we do not hesitate to command openly: let us fast, brothers and sisters, lest perhaps tomorrow we die. Openly let us claim our disciplines. We are certain that those who are in the flesh cannot please God, not indeed in the substance of flesh, but in care, but in affection, but in operation, but in will. Leanness does not displease us; for God has not given flesh by weight, just as neither spirit by measure. More easily, if perhaps, through the narrow gate of salvation will enter the thinner flesh; more quickly will be raised the lighter flesh, longer in the tomb will last the drier flesh. Let boxers and Olympic fighters be fattened. To them ambition of body is fitting, to whom also strength is necessary, and yet they too grow strong by dry-food fasts. But ours are other strengths and other powers, just as also other contests, for whom the struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the powers of the world, against spiritual forces of wickedness. Against these it is necessary to stand not with flesh and blood, but with faith and a robust spirit. Otherwise a fatter Christian will be necessary to bears and lions perhaps rather than to God, except that also against beasts he ought to practice leanness.

pass_b_english: You are old, if we want to speak the truth: you who indulge so much in gluttony, and rightly you boast that you are first. I always recognize the taste of Esau the hunter of wild beasts in you. So you devote yourself everywhere to tracking down thrushes, so you come in from the field of your utterly undisciplined way of life, so you grow faint in spirit. If I offer you lentil stew reddened with reduced wine, you will immediately sell all your birthrights.

Among you the love-feast boils in pots, faith is warmed at the hearth, hope is spread out on serving dishes. But the love-feast is the greater thing, because through it your young men recline with the sisters. These are, of course, the appendages of gluttony: wantonness and luxuries. The apostle knew this association when, after first saying not in drunkenness nor in revelings, he added nor in beds and lusts (Romans 13:13). It belongs to the indictment of your gluttony that among you a double honor for those who preside is assigned in double portions of food, when the apostle gave double honor to both brothers and leaders (1 Timothy 5:17). Who is holier among you than the one who feasts more often, who provides more lavish banquets, who is better equipped with drinking cups?

Rightly do you who are people of soul and flesh alone reject spiritual things. If the prophets pleased such people, they would not be mine. Why then do you not openly proclaim: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die (1 Corinthians 15:32)? Just as we do not hesitate to command openly: Let us fast, brothers and sisters, lest perhaps tomorrow we die. Let us openly defend our disciplines.

We are certain that those who are in the flesh cannot please God (Romans 8:8)—not, of course, in the substance of the flesh, but in its care, in its affection, in its activity, in its will. Leanness does not displease us. For God did not give the flesh by weight, just as he did not give the Spirit by measure. More easily, perhaps, will the thinner flesh enter through the narrow gate of salvation (Matthew 7:13-14); more quickly will the lighter flesh be raised; longer will the drier flesh endure in the tomb.

Let the boxers and Olympic wrestlers be fattened. Ambition of the body suits those who also need strength—and yet even they grow strong on dry-food fasts. But our strengths are different, and our powers are different, just as our contests are different. For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the powers of the world, against spiritual forces of wickedness (Ephesians 6:12). Against these one must stand not with flesh and blood, but with faith and a strong spirit. Besides, a fatter Christian will perhaps be more useful to bears and lions than to God—except that even against wild beasts he will need to practice leanness.

last_rejected.ruling: 'Sapere' can mean 'to taste/savor'; rendering 'recognize the taste' is within normal range, not a major error.

fixed: faith grows warm on stalks of grain, hope lies flat on serving dishes: source 'fides in culmis calet, spes in ferculis iacet' — 'culmis' means stalks of grain, but the metaphor is that faith and hope are reduced to food at love-feasts; 'warmed at the hearth' and 'spread out on serving dishes' better conveys the sense that faith and hope are reduced to food at love-feasts.

the love-feast is the greater thing, because through it your young men sleep with the sisters: source 'adulescentes tui cum sororibus dormiunt' — 'dormiunt' can mean 'sleep' or 'recline'; in context of a love-feast meal, 'recline' is more accurate and avoids implying sexual relations.
